{{Short description|Darts tournament}} {{Infobox individual darts tournament |tournament_name = 2026 Machineseeker European Championship |image = |dates = 22–25 October 2026 |venue = [[Westfalenhallen]] |location = [[Dortmund]], Germany |organisation = [[Professional Darts Corporation]] (PDC) |format = [[Leg (darts)|Legs]] |prize_fund = £750,000 |winners_share = £150,000 |nine_dart = [[Luke Woodhouse]] |high_checkout = '''167''' [[Martin Schindler]] |winner = '''{{flagathlete|[[Ross Smith (darts player)|Ross Smith]]|ENG}}''' |prev = [[2025 European Championship (darts)|2025]] |next = [[2027 European Championship (darts)|2027]] }} The '''2026 European Championship''' (known for sponsorship reasons as the '''2026 Machineseeker European Championship''') was a professional [[darts]] tournament held at the [[Westfalenhallen]] in [[Dortmund]], Germany, from 22 to 25 October 2026. It was the 19th staging of the [[European Championship (darts)|European Championship]] by the [[Professional Darts Corporation]] (PDC). The total prize fund was £750,000, with the winner receiving £150,000. The tournament featured the top 32 players based on ranking money earned in the 15 [[PDC European Tour|European Tour]] events that were held as part of the [[2026 PDC Pro Tour]]. [[Gian van Veen]] was the defending champion, having defeated [[Luke Humphries]] 11–10 in the [[2025 European Championship (darts)|2025 final]], but he lost 10–6 to [[Luke Woodhouse]] in the second round. Woodhouse also hit a [[nine-dart finish]] in the fourth leg of his first round match against [[Dirk van Duijvenbode]]. [[Kevin Doets]] and [[Niels Zonneveld]] made their debuts at the tournament. [[Ross Smith (darts player)|Ross Smith]] won the tournament, his third major title and second European Championship, by defeating [[Martin Schindler]] 11–8 in the final. Schindler also became the first German player to reach the final of a PDC major. ==Overview== ===Prize money=== The prize fund increased to £750,000, with £150,000 going to the winner.
